spec.title: The gate that blocks the bad change
spec.intro:
Module 01 asked a live machine "is this disk encrypted?" and kept the answer. This lab
asks the same claim-class question — is storage encrypted at rest, and never public —
against the CODE that will create the storage, before anything exists. Your workspace
is the CI pipeline's working directory, staged exactly as `bash labs/setup.sh ./lab08`
leaves it: the proposed Terraform change, the scanner's structured result for it, the
control map you own, and the gate. The "Run validator" button IS the pipeline's gate
step — it runs `gate.sh lab08/scan-under-gate.json lab08/control-map.csv HIGH`, a port
of the committed gate.sh verified byte-for-byte in CI against real bash runs of the
same script, so the record and exit code you see here are the ones a real machine
produces. `lab08/scan-under-gate.json` is the scan step's output for the change under
review; this pipeline pins its severity floor at HIGH (one owned value in its config —
the MEDIUM-floor exploration runs on your own machine with the lab's setup script).

tasks.instruction:
Before running anything, read `lab08/main-noncompliant.tf` and predict which of the
three control questions (encryption / public access / versioning) the declared
resources fail. Then open `lab08/checkov-noncompliant.json` and reconcile your
prediction with the scanner's failed checks. Record the result in section 1 of
`lab08/findings-worksheet.md` — one line per question, in the worksheet's format,
with the scanner's check id and severity.

hints.nudge: The violation is what the declaration is MISSING. The .tf declares a bucket and a public-read ACL — which question does each line answer, and which questions are answered by silence?

hints.concept: §4.1 — absence in the declaration is the violation; §4.2 — every rule has a stable identifier and a severity

hints.reveal: encryption: FAIL CKV_AWS_19 HIGH · public-access: FAIL CKV_AWS_20 HIGH · versioning: FAIL CKV_AWS_21 MEDIUM

tasks.explain:
You answered a control question by reading text — no cloud account, no console,
nothing provisioned. All three rules fail, including the MEDIUM versioning gap the
worked example's summary tends to overshadow. That is the whole opening of this
module: the bucket-that-will-exist is a file you can check at the speed of opening it.

tasks.instruction:
Run the gate: click "Run validator" — the pipeline's gate step, evaluating the scan
result at the HIGH floor. Confirm the decision is FAIL with exit code 1: that
non-zero exit is the entire enforcement — the build system refuses the merge. Then
keep the verdict: copy the gate's complete output into `lab08/gate-block-record.txt`,
replacing the placeholder line.

verify.regex: ^GATE_DECISION: FAIL  \(build blocked — 2 control\(s\) violated at/above HIGH\)$

hints.nudge: Run validator IS `bash gate.sh lab08/scan-under-gate.json lab08/control-map.csv HIGH`. Watch the exit code under the output — 1 means blocked. The record itself is evidence: keep all of it.

hints.concept: §4.5 — any blocking finding ⇒ non-zero exit ⇒ no merge

hints.reveal: Click Run validator (decision: FAIL, exit 1), then copy its full output into lab08/gate-block-record.txt in place of the placeholder line

tasks.explain:
Two HIGH findings blocked; the MEDIUM one was recorded but did not block. Nothing
was created wrong, because the wrongness was caught while it was still text. A
detection sits in a report; this exit code physically refuses to let the bad change
exist — that is the difference between detection and enforcement.

tasks.instruction:
Read your block record as an auditor: each blocking FAILED line names both the
scanner's rule id and the control it enforces. In section 2 of the worksheet, map
each blocking finding to its named control. Then open `lab08/control-map.csv` —
the file that performed that translation — and notice it is yours: versioned,
reviewable, and independent of the scanner vendor.

verify.regex: ^FAILED  CKV_AWS_19  \[HIGH\]  -> SC-28 \(Protection of Information at Rest\)  : BLOCK$

hints.nudge: The block record already speaks both languages on each FAILED line: tool-speak (CKV_…) to the left of the arrow, auditor-speak (SC-… / AC-…) to the right. The bridge is one CSV you own.

hints.concept: §4.3 — the control map is policy-as-data: the map is yours, the scanner is just the sensor

hints.reveal: Worksheet section 2: CKV_AWS_19 -> SC-28 and CKV_AWS_20 -> AC-3 — both mappings appear verbatim in the gate's block record

tasks.explain:
`CKV_AWS_19` is a vendor's rule name; "SC-28, Protection of Information at Rest" is
a control with an owner an auditor recognises. The one-row-per-rule CSV that joins
them is the most GRC-specific artifact in this pipeline — when the catalogue changes,
you change that file, in version control, with a reviewer.

tasks.instruction:
Diagnose the fix before shipping it: read `lab08/main-compliant.tf` and, in section 3
of the worksheet, point to what remediates each blocking finding — which block or
setting answers the encryption question, and which clears public access.

hints.nudge: Diff the two .tf files in your head: which blocks exist only in main-compliant.tf? One declares encryption at rest; one line changes who can read the bucket.

hints.concept: §5.3 — remediation makes the scanner's questions answerable with yes, in the declaration itself

hints.reveal: CKV_AWS_19 fixed by: the aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration block (sse_algorithm aws:kms) · CKV_AWS_20 fixed by: acl = "private" in aws_s3_bucket_acl

tasks.explain:
Diagnosing a blocked build is exactly this walk: the gate names the finding, the map
names the control, and the fix is a visible diff in the declaration. The author
doesn't negotiate with the gate — they change the text until the questions answer yes.

tasks.instruction:
Ship the remediation. The scanner's re-run against the fixed change is the committed
`lab08/checkov-compliant.json` — make the pipeline's scan step reflect it by replacing
the ENTIRE contents of `lab08/scan-under-gate.json` with that file's contents
(copy the whole file). Run the gate again and confirm the decision is PASS with exit
code 0. Then capture the evidence: copy the complete PASS record into
`lab08/evidence-storage-controls.txt`, replacing the placeholder.

hints.nudge: The gate evaluates whatever the scan step last produced — scan-under-gate.json. Replace its whole contents with checkov-compliant.json's (select all, copy, paste), run, and keep the gate's own PASS record.

hints.concept: §4.6 — the evidence is generated by the control, not asserted about it; a record the gate emits cannot drift from what the gate did

hints.reveal: Copy ALL of lab08/checkov-compliant.json into lab08/scan-under-gate.json, click Run validator (PASS, exit 0), then copy the full output into lab08/evidence-storage-controls.txt

tasks.explain:
The same gate that blocked the bad change just emitted the proof that SC-28 and AC-3
were evaluated and held on this one — failed_checks_evaluated: 0, nothing at or above
the floor. Because the record is a byproduct of the enforcement, it cannot lie about
what happened: that file is the EVALUATE stage's output handed forward to EVIDENCE.

tasks.instruction:
The severity floor is a risk decision written as one value. This pipeline pins its
floor at HIGH; on your own machine, run the lab's gate with the floor lowered —
`bash labs/setup.sh ./lab08`, then `bash lab08/gate.sh lab08/checkov-noncompliant.json
lab08/control-map.csv MEDIUM` — or reason it through from the block record you kept.
In 2–4 sentences: what changes in the decision at a MEDIUM floor, why, and where in
your owned files a real organisation would record that risk-appetite change so it is
reviewable.

hints.nudge: At HIGH, CKV_AWS_21 (CP-9, versioning) was recorded but did not block. Rank the severities: what crosses the line when the line moves to MEDIUM?

hints.concept: §4.4 — the floor is risk appetite expressed as code, and changing it is itself a reviewable diff

tasks.instruction:
The lab's written deliverable, in 4–6 sentences for a colleague who has never written
Terraform: what declaring infrastructure as text made checkable, and when; why the
non-compliant change was blocked and what the exit code meant to the build system
(enforcement, not detection); why mapping each finding to a named control matters and
why the control map — not the scanner — is the artifact a GRC engineer owns; and why
the gate-emitted PASS record cannot drift from reality. If you do the optional
real-environment task, describe where the scanner and the gate sit in the workflow
so a non-zero gate exit blocks the merge.

hints.nudge: Walk the five parts of §3 in order: declare → scan → map → gate → evidence. The bucket is never created wrong, because the wrongness was caught while it was still text.

hints.concept: §3 — The Mental Model: where, exactly, does a control fail?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gate.sh — the CORE LOGIC of the §6 lab, isolated for testing.
#
# Reads a Checkov-shaped JSON scan result and a control map, applies a severity
# floor, maps every failed check to the control it enforces, decides PASS/FAIL,
# and emits a machine- and auditor-readable evidence record on stdout.
#
# This is the EVALUATE step of the loop expressed as code. It is deliberately
# free of network, cloud, and scanner dependencies: it consumes a scan result
# that some scanner already produced. In the real pipeline the scanner runs
# first; here we prove the gate decision against committed fixtures.
#
# Usage:   gate.sh <checkov-result.json> <control-map.csv> [severity-floor]
# Default severity-floor: HIGH
# Exit:    0 = control set PASSES (build proceeds)
#          1 = control set FAILS  (build blocked)
#          2 = usage / input error
#
# Dependencies: bash + coreutils + awk only. No jq, no network.
set -euo pipefail

RESULT="${1:-}"
CONTROL_MAP="${2:-}"
FLOOR="${3:-HIGH}"

if [ -z "$RESULT" ] || [ -z "$CONTROL_MAP" ]; then
  echo "usage: gate.sh <checkov-result.json> <control-map.csv> [severity-floor]" >&2
  exit 2
fi
[ -f "$RESULT" ]      || { echo "ERROR: scan result not found: $RESULT" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$CONTROL_MAP" ] || { echo "ERROR: control map not found: $CONTROL_MAP" >&2; exit 2; }

# Rank severities so the floor is a numeric comparison, not a string match.
sev_rank() {
  case "$1" in
    CRITICAL) echo 4 ;;
    HIGH)     echo 3 ;;
    MEDIUM)   echo 2 ;;
    LOW)      echo 1 ;;
    *)        echo 0 ;;
  esac
}
FLOOR_RANK="$(sev_rank "$FLOOR")"
[ "$FLOOR_RANK" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: unknown severity floor: $FLOOR" >&2; exit 2; }

# Extract failed checks from the JSON. We do NOT require jq: the relevant fields
# (check_id, check_name, severity) appear as quoted "key": "value" pairs, and
# every failed check is an object inside the "failed_checks" array. A single awk
# pass tracks bracket/brace depth so it isolates exactly the failed_checks array
# (correctly stepping over nested arrays like "file_line_range": [1, 4]), then
# emits one tab-separated record per object: check_id, severity, check_name.
#
# This is a pragmatic parser for THIS well-formed, machine-generated shape, not
# a general JSON parser. The real lab pipes real scanner output through jq; the
# fixture parser keeps the happy path dependency-free.
extract_failed() {
  awk '
    BEGIN { instr = 0; arm = 0; depth = 0; arraydepth = 0; objbuf = "" }
    {
      line = $0
      # If this line names the failed_checks key, arm so the next "[" opens
      # our array. The "[" can be on the same line, so arm before scanning.
      if (line ~ /"failed_checks"[ \t]*:/) arm = 1
      n = length(line)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr(line, i, 1)
        prev = (i > 1) ? substr(line, i-1, 1) : ""
        # String-literal tracking so structural chars inside strings dont count.
        if (c == "\"" && prev != "\\") { instr = !instr }

        # Buffer EVERY char while we are inside a top-level object of the array,
        # including string content (we need the field values).
        if (collecting) objbuf = objbuf c

        if (instr) continue   # only structure decisions below ignore strings

        if (c == "[") {
          depth++
          if (arm == 1) { arraydepth = depth; arm = 0 }
        } else if (c == "]") {
          if (arraydepth && depth == arraydepth) arraydepth = 0
          depth--
        } else if (c == "{") {
          if (arraydepth && depth == arraydepth && !collecting) {
            collecting = 1; objbuf = "{"; objlevel = 0
          }
          if (collecting) objlevel++
        } else if (c == "}") {
          if (collecting) {
            objlevel--
            if (objlevel == 0) {
              cid = field(objbuf, "check_id")
              sev = field(objbuf, "severity")
              nm  = field(objbuf, "check_name")
              if (cid != "") {
                if (sev == "") sev = "UNKNOWN"
                if (nm  == "") nm  = "unknown"
                printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n", cid, sev, nm
              }
              collecting = 0; objbuf = ""
            }
          }
        }
      }
      if (collecting) objbuf = objbuf "\n"
    }
    function field(s, key,   re, m) {
      re = "\"" key "\"[ \t]*:[ \t]*\"[^\"]*\""
      if (match(s, re)) {
        m = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        sub(/^.*:[ \t]*"/, "", m)
        sub(/"$/, "", m)
        return m
      }
      return ""
    }
  ' "$RESULT"
}

# Look a check_id up in the control map; print "control_id|control_title" or "UNMAPPED".
map_control() {
  awk -F, -v want="$1" '
    NR == 1 { next }                      # skip header
    $1 == want { print $2 "|" $3; found=1; exit }
    END { if (!found) print "UNMAPPED|unmapped check (no control owner)" }
  ' "$CONTROL_MAP"
}

echo "=== GRC IaC Gate — evidence record ==="
echo "scan_result: $RESULT"
echo "control_map: $CONTROL_MAP"
echo "severity_floor: $FLOOR"
echo "evaluated_at: ${GATE_FAKE_TIME:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)}"
echo "---"

BLOCKING=0
EVALUATED=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r cid sev name; do
  [ -n "${cid:-}" ] || continue
  EVALUATED=$((EVALUATED + 1))
  rank="$(sev_rank "$sev")"
  mapping="$(map_control "$cid")"
  control_id="${mapping%%|*}"
  control_title="${mapping#*|}"
  if [ "$rank" -ge "$FLOOR_RANK" ]; then
    verdict="BLOCK"
    BLOCKING=$((BLOCKING + 1))
  else
    verdict="below-floor (not blocking)"
  fi
  echo "FAILED  $cid  [$sev]  -> $control_id ($control_title)  : $verdict"
  echo "        $name"
done < <(extract_failed)

echo "---"
echo "failed_checks_evaluated: $EVALUATED"
echo "blocking_at_or_above_${FLOOR}: $BLOCKING"

if [ "$BLOCKING" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "GATE_DECISION: FAIL  (build blocked — $BLOCKING control(s) violated at/above $FLOOR)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "GATE_DECISION: PASS  (no violations at/above $FLOOR — build proceeds, evidence emitted)"
exit 0
